title: 🗄️ Code-Execution Flaws in Famous Databases… and the Updates Have Arrived!
body: 🗄️ Code-Execution Flaws in Famous Databases… and the Updates Have Arrived!

A security researcher revealed a series of flaws that let low-privilege accounts run code on the database server itself. The list includes a type-confusion flaw in PostgreSQL numbered CVE-2026-116331 and fixed on November 12, a flaw in the MySQL query optimizer numbered CVE-2026-101786 and fixed on October 20, a flaw in Oracle Text rated 9.9 out of 10 numbered CVE-2026-114819 and fixed on November 17, plus an unauthenticated series in ORDS GraphQL numbered CVE-2026-91609 and fixed on October 20, and an integer-overflow flaw in ClickHouse fixed in version 26.9 and later. Exploitation proofs were published on November 18, and no real attacks have been observed so far.
Simply put: a database is not just a store for information; a flaw in it could hand the attacker the keys to the whole server, and the latest updates close these gaps.
Do you apply database updates as soon as they come out?
